To: Pat Staffer <pat@yourcompany.com>
Subject: Following up: commercial lending partnership

 

CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organization. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognize the sender and know the content is safe.

 

Pat,

 

As promised after our call, here is a fuller read on where we are seeing the market heading into year end, and where we think a partnership on the commercial side could make sense for both of us.

 

Deposit pricing. After two years of paying up for deposits, most regional and trust banks in our peer group have started to let promotional rates roll off. Our own cost of interest-bearing deposits peaked in the second quarter and has come down about 18 basis points since. That gives us room to price term loans more competitively than we could in the spring, particularly for borrowers who bring operating accounts with them. We are not chasing volume for its own sake, but relationship pricing is back on the table.

 

Commercial real estate. The maturity wall is real, but it is uneven. Office remains the problem segment and we are not adding exposure there. Industrial, multifamily with stabilized occupancy, and owner-occupied properties are all areas where we still have appetite. For owner-occupied deals we can go to 80 percent loan-to-value with a full recourse guaranty, and we can hold up to 15 million on our balance sheet before needing a participant. Above that we have a group of four participant banks we syndicate with regularly.

 

Equipment and fleet. This is where we see the most overlap with your book. We can take titled collateral, provide lines with a borrowing base tied to orderly liquidation values, and close in roughly 30 days from a complete package. We prefer borrowers with at least three years of audited or reviewed financials and a fixed-charge coverage ratio above 1.25 times. We are flexible on amortization for newer equipment and can structure seasonal payment schedules where the cash flow supports it.

 

Credit process. Every request goes through a two-step review: a screening memo within five business days and a full committee decision within three weeks of receiving the package. For referred deals we assign a single relationship manager from day one so the borrower is not passed between teams. Our committee meets weekly, so timing rarely depends on calendars.

 

Referral arrangement. We are open to a standard referral agreement and to co-lending where your clients need more capacity than one balance sheet can hold. We do not pay referral fees on consumer products, but on commercial credits we can discuss terms once we have a sense of the expected volume. I have copied the outline we use with other partners into our standard term sheet, which I can send over once your counsel is ready to look at it.

 

What would help us most is a short list of the kinds of deals you see that do not fit your current lenders, ideally with rough sizes and collateral types. That will let me tell you quickly which ones we can do and which ones we would pass on, so nobody wastes time.

 

Happy to get together in person next time I am in Nashville; I am usually there once a month.

 

Best regards,

 

Harper Lindqvist

Director, Capital Markets

Stonebridge Trust Company

One Federal Street, 22nd Floor

Boston, MA 02110
